worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \frac{10}{(t+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =10\int (t+1)^{-2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =10\cdot \frac{(t+1)^{-1}}{-1}+C \\  & =-\frac{10}{t+1}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $x(0)=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =-\frac{10}{0+1}+C \\ 4 & =-10+C \\ C & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=-\frac{10}{t+1}+14.
$$
